fact: SeyLII records the National Payment System Act, 2014 (Act 14 of 2014) as assented to on 11 August 2014 and published and commenced on 18 August 2014, with later amendments by the 2022 e-money regulations and the 2023 amending Act.

The National Payment System (Electronic Money) Regulations, 2022 (S.I. 128 of 2022), made by the Central Bank under section 42(1) of the National Payment System Act, 2014, commenced on 12 December 2022.

The 2022 e-money regulations set capital (SCR 1,000,000 initial) and liquidity rules for electronic money issuers other than banks, and treat issuers that are banks, credit unions or other issuers as separate cases, so non-bank issuers operate under them.

The Central Bank of Seychelles made the National Payment System (Licensing and Authorisation) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025 (S.I. 99 of 2025) on 15 December 2025 under the National Payment System Act, 2014 (Act 14 of 2014), amending the 2014 licensing regulations; they take effect on the 30th day after Gazette publication.

fact: The 2025 amendment to regulation 9 sets the conditions on which the Central Bank may license a payment service provider, any company incorporated under the Companies Act, while regulation 17 as amended exempts banks and credit unions only from annual fees, and regulation 20(d) as amended refers to electronic money institutions safeguarding holders' funds at licensed banks.
